advances: This gives an exact comparison and a conditional first-order lower bound for the optimized normalized value at a fixed buffer scale.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write $q_t=Q_t(U_t)$. The conditions of 569a05581be52e0e apply along every sequence $t\to0$ because $M_t\to M>0$ and the raw near-minimality error is at most $M_tt^2$. In particular $q_t\to Q$, the sampled maxima of $U_t$ have a common bound, the parameters converge to $L$ locally uniformly in each limiting own interior, and their zero-extended logarithms converge in mixed $L^1$. The uniform maxima bound is established in the proof of that fact. Taking a constant body and a sequence of near-minimizers also shows that $Q/M=v(0)$. The old source marks are own-interior by that fact. A common inner homothety exists by the old inball and Hausdorff support comparison in its proof. The pushed means satisfy $Y_i^t=(p_i,(1-a_t)y_i+a_t\int g_Z\,d\rho_i)$ and belong to the actual current $p_i$-fiber by compatibility. Their old interior limits ensure they lie in the new own interiors for all small $t$.

For fixed $s\ge0$, $B_i(t,s)\to B_i(0,s)$ by the all-tilt slab comparison in 569a05581be52e0e and joint energy continuity b3c0088cf09b2894. The same argument gives continuity in $s$. The base values converge, since they are minima of finitely many base-trace weights. For any fixed current body and its interior mark, $B_i(t,s)$ is nondecreasing and strictly increasing below the atomic value: if a larger positive scalar is still below it, use a proper minimizing cap from 20210aa9d661295a at that scalar. Moving its threshold back to the smaller scalar removes positive own mass and weakly decreases all other masses, so the smaller scalar has strictly smaller infimum. At a large enough scalar the full own fiber is captured by every nonvertical normal, and 3dd858960f824a5d shows the depth then equals atomic depth. At $t=0$, $B_i(0,L_i)=Q$ and $L_i>0$. Removing the old positive shift from an old proper minimizing cap removes positive own mass, so $B_i(0,0)<Q$. These arguments apply also in base rank zero with the whole-base trace. Choose fixed $0<s_i^-<L_i<s_i^+$ with their old depths strictly below and strictly above $Q$, respectively. Fixed-scalar convergence and the fixed strict atomic gaps then give a common closed interval $J$ about $Q$ in the open depth ranges for all small $t$, and ensure that every inverse lies in $[s_i^-,s_i^+]$. A comparison with two fixed scalars arbitrarily close to each old inverse gives $s_i(t,q_t')\to s_i(0,q')$ whenever $q_t'\to q'\in J$. In particular $H_t$ is continuous strictly increasing on $J$, and its range contains a fixed neighborhood of zero for all small $t$.

Concave Jensen for each pushed probability gives $U_t(Y_i^t)/L_i\ge\int U_t(T_tw)/L_i\,d\rho_i$. Apply logarithmic Jensen to the right hand side in the form $\log(\int R\,d\bar\rho_i)\ge\int\log R\,d\bar\rho_i$, where $R=U_t(T_tw)/L(w)$ and $d\bar\rho_i=(L/L_i)d\rho_i$. The $L$-moment makes $\bar\rho_i$ a probability and the certificate gives $\sum_i\sigma_i\bar\rho_i=dm/M$. Thus
$$
\sum_i\sigma_i\log[U_t(Y_i^t)/L_i]\ge\frac1M\int_S\log R\,dm=\xi_t.
$$
For the equality, the old log mean is zero and the common fiber Jacobian $j_t$ changes the integral of $\log U_t\circ T_t$ to $j_t^{-1}$ times the integral of $\log U_t$ over the images. The new log mean is zero, so this is minus the collar integral. The collar volume tends to zero by volume convergence and $j_t\to1$. The zero-extended log convergence gives $\xi_t\to0$ by absolute continuity of the integral of the limiting logarithm. For small $t$ the mark depth is at most $q_t\in J$, so strict inversion below base depth gives $U_t(Y_i^t)\le s_i(t,q_t)$ for every $i$. This proves both exact comparisons.

The common upper bound gives the first one-sided collar bound and hence the first value lower envelope by monotonicity of $\chi_t$. A reference can be obtained by old-fiber nearest-point projection followed by $L$. Any reference satisfying the given convergence has a common positive floor for small $t$ by compactness and the old positive floor. To prove the positive-part bound, take any sampled sequence $X_t\to X$ in a fixed limiting fiber on which an upward gap persisted. At an interior limit, local uniform convergence rules it out. At a boundary limit choose $g\in\operatorname{int}K_z$ and fix $0<s<1$. The points $(1-s)g+sX_t$ are eventually in a fixed interior core. Concavity gives
$$
U_t(z,X_t)\le [U_t(z,(1-s)g+sX_t)-(1-s)U_t(z,g)]/s .
$$
First pass to the limit at the two interior arguments and then let $s\uparrow1$, using continuity of $L$ at $X$. This proves $\limsup U_t(z,X_t)\le L(z,X)$ and excludes the gap. The reference floor gives $\log U_t\le\log L_{\rm ref,t}+o(1)$ uniformly, and integrating this on the collar proves the sharpened estimate. The strict inverse also has a uniform lower slope in the $q$ variable for $H_t$ on $J$. On the positive compact intervals of inverse scalars the displacement as a function of $\log s$ is uniformly Lipschitz, and the all-tilt slab bound then gives $B_i(t,s_2)-B_i(t,s_1)\le C_i(\log s_2-\log s_1)$ for $s_2\ge s_1$. Substitute the inverses and sum with weights to obtain $H_t(q_2)-H_t(q_1)\ge(\sum_i\sigma_i/C_i)(q_2-q_1)$. This estimate requires no first-order expansion.

For the radial claim, $H_z(X)$ is positive almost everywhere by the centroidal inball. The collar on an old ray is the radial parameter interval from $b_{z,t}(X)$ to $a_t$, and containment gives $b_{z,t}(X)\le a_t$. In the parametrization $g_z+(1-s)(X-g_z)$ the volume element is $(1-s)^{d-1}H_z(X)dS\,ds$. This follows from the tangential derivatives on the Lipschitz convex boundary charts and the radial derivative $-(X-g_z)$. For $d=1$ it is the endpoint interval length formula with counting surface measure. Both endpoints are $O(t)$, and reference log values differ from $\log L(z,X)$ by $o(1)$ uniformly along these radial intervals by compactness. Dividing by $t$ and using bounded convergence on each boundary gives the collar limit with factor $cH_z-v_z\ge0$. The error $o(h_t)$ is $o(t)$ since the uniformly bounded radial widths give $h_t=O(t)$. This proves the signed one-sided inequality.

Finally, if $r<(c_0-B_0)/A_0$, the assumed expansion and the collar lower limit give $H_t(Q+tr)<\xi_t\le H_t(q_t)$ eventually, so $q_t>Q+tr$. Let $r$ increase to $(c_0-B_0)/A_0$ for the raw lower bound. Use $v(t)\ge q_t/M_t-t^2$, the assumed mass expansion, and $q_t\to Q$ to obtain the normalized lower bound.
statement:
Assume the actual compatible fixed-base bodies and old positive continuous log-normalized parameter $L$ satisfy the finite volume certificate hypotheses of 569a05581be52e0e at a fixed $\varepsilon>0$. In particular the contact probabilities $\rho_i$ have weights $\sigma_i>0$ summing to one, full means $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ and $L$-means $L_i=L(Y_i)$, and $\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\rho_i=dm/(ML)$. Each $Y_i$ is an old maximizing mark with raw depth $Q$, strictly below its closed pure-base depth. Let $K_z(t)\to K_z$ be positive compatible bodies in the fixed-base fiber Hausdorff topology as $t\downarrow0$, with mixed volume $dm_t$ and total $M_t$. Define $v(t)=\inf_U Q_t(U)/M_t$ over current positive continuous concave, log-normalized parameters. Choose $U_t$ with $Q_t(U_t)/M_t\le v(t)+t^2$.

Choose a common inward fractional contraction $a_t\to0$, $0\le a_t<1$, of the old fibers about their old centroids $g_z$ so that its image $I_{t,z}$ is contained in $K_z(t)$. Let $T_t(z,X)=(z,g_z+(1-a_t)(X-g_z))$ and $j_t=(1-a_t)^d$. Let $Y_i^t$ be the mean of $(T_t)_\#\rho_i$, and $B_i(t,s)$ its actual raw buffered depth with scalar parameter value $s$. On a common interval of raw depths about $Q$, for all sufficiently small $t$ there is a unique positive inverse $s_i(t,q)$ of this scalar depth. Define $H_t(q)=\sum_i\sigma_i\log(s_i(t,q)/L_i)$ and let $\chi_t$ denote its local inverse. If
$$
\xi_t=-\frac1{Mj_t}\sum_z\int_{K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}}\log U_t\,dX,
$$
then $H_t(Q_t(U_t))\ge\xi_t$ and $Q_t(U_t)\ge\chi_t(\xi_t)$.

Let $h_t=\sum_z|K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}|$ and let $B\ge1$ be a common sampled upper bound for $U_t$. Then $\xi_t\ge-h_t\log B/(Mj_t)$ and $v(t)\ge\chi_t(-h_t\log B/(Mj_t))/M_t-t^2$. More precisely, for positive continuous reference values $L_{\rm ref,t}$ on the sampled moving fibers that converge to $L$ along all convergent sampled marks, we have $\sup_{S_t}(U_t-L_{\rm ref,t})_+\to0$ and
$$
\xi_t\ge-\frac1{Mj_t}\sum_z\int_{K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}}\log L_{\rm ref,t}\,dX+o(h_t).
$$
If the moving endpoint on the ray through a regular old boundary point $X$ from $g_z$ is $g_z+(1-b_{z,t}(X))(X-g_z)$, assume $|b_{z,t}(X)|=O(t)$ uniformly and $b_{z,t}(X)/t\to v_z(X)/[n_z(X)\cdot(X-g_z)]$ surface-almost everywhere, where $v_z$ is a bounded measurable signed inward speed. With $a_t=ct+o(t)$ and $H_z(X)=n_z(X)\cdot(X-g_z)$, containment gives $cH_z-v_z\ge0$ and
$$
\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\xi_t}{t}\ge
c_{\rm col}:=\frac1M\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\log L(z,X)[v_z(X)-cH_z(X)]\,dS.
$$

If, independently, $H_t(Q+tr)=t(A_0 r+B_0)+o(t)$ uniformly for bounded $r$, with $A_0>0$, and $\liminf\xi_t/t\ge c_0$, then $\liminf (Q_t(U_t)-Q)/t\ge(c_0-B_0)/A_0$. If also $M_t=M-tD+o(t)$, then
$$
\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{v(t)-Q/M}{t}
\ge\frac{(c_0-B_0)/A_0+(Q/M)D}{M}.
$$
title: Weighted scalar lower comparison for optimized buffered depth
